_comment: Betting-market team strength, used as a prior on the season projection.
Copy to rosters/market_odds_<target_year>.json and edit. The market is the
best single forward-looking read on team talent available: it knows
front-office intent, depth behind the starters, managerial quality, spring
injuries, and every signing that has not produced a stat line yet -- none
of which a roster aggregate can see.
WHICH MARKET, best to worst:
1. win_total     Season win-total lines (over/under 88.5). A DIRECT read
on expected wins, no inference needed. Use these if you
can get them.
2. pennant       League-championship odds. One playoff round removed.
3. world_series  Title futures. Usable, but the loosest of the three: a
championship is four short series deep, so playoff
randomness compresses the board. Even the best team in
baseball wins the title only 15-20% of the time, so the
top of the board SATURATES and carries less information
about talent than the middle does.
That is why futures prices are used for their ORDERING and relative
spacing, with the absolute scale taken from MLB's own long-run win
distribution (mean exactly 81, SD ~11.5). See
market_odds.implied_wins_from_probabilities.
WHAT IT FEEDS:
wins -> save and hold opportunity pools (team_wins.py)
wins -> run differential -> the RS/RA magnitude
It does NOT set the RS/RA split. A 95-win club could be 5.2 RS / 4.2 RA or
4.3 / 3.3 and the futures price is identical. The market supplies the
magnitude of the run differential; the bottom-up roster factors supply how
it divides between offense and defense.
FIELDS:
market        'world_series' (default), 'pennant', 'division', or
'win_total'. With 'win_total', `teams` holds the line
itself and no inference runs.
odds_format   'american' (+450 / -150), 'decimal' (5.50), or
'probability' (0.18, or 18 for a percentage). Ignored for
a win_total market.
teams         team code -> price or line. Any code canonical_team()
understands works. Give ALL 30 clubs: a partial board
warns, because the teams left out fall back to the
bottom-up projection and the two scales then mix.
as_of / book  free text, for provenance. Record when you pulled the
board and from where -- futures move a lot across an
offseason and a stale board is worse than none.
KNOWN BIASES, neither of which this file corrects:
* Favorite-longshot bias -- longshots are overbet, so their de-vigged
probability overstates their real chance. The default 'power' de-vig
pushes back on this; 'proportional' does not.
* Public teams -- large-market clubs carry shorter prices than talent
alone justifies. Read a big-market club's market-implied wins as a
mild over-estimate.
The numbers below are ILLUSTRATIVE PLACEHOLDERS to show the shape and
rough magnitude of a real board. They are not a forecast and are not
pulled from any book. Replace all 30 before using this.
book: REPLACE-ME (e.g. consensus, or a specific book)
